ai.headline: Prince Harry says he hopes to mend ties with his father and brother
ai.summary:
Prince Harry, the Duke of Sussex, has said he wants to repair his strained relationship with King Charles and Prince William. In an interview with GQ magazine, conducted the previous month and published as the royal family hosted the Sultan of Oman at Windsor Castle, he described family rifts as a common experience that many people find relatable. He said he hoped the reconciliation would happen and called it the most important priority, while also saying that some past hurts are hard to let go of. A spokesperson for the Sussexes later said his remarks were not meant as a jab at William or any other royal family member.

Harry also explained why he and his wife, Meghan Markle, moved back to Britain. He said the chance to enroll their children in British schools was a major factor, and that the family had been there for about two weeks when he spoke. He described his children, Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five, as gaining a different cultural experience. Harry also spoke about grief and therapy after his mother's death, saying he did not want public sympathy and hoped that sharing his story would help others. Separately, British broadcaster Piers Morgan criticized Harry's comments on Fox News, calling them hypocritical and arguing that the couple's public criticism of the royal family had faded from attention.
key_points: Prince Harry said he wants to repair his relationship with King Charles and Prince William, according to a GQ interview.
The interview was conducted last month and released as the Sultan of Oman visited Windsor Castle for a state visit.
A spokesperson for the Sussexes said the comments were not aimed at William or any royal family member.
Harry said the couple returned to Britain partly so their children could attend British schools; he has two children, Archie and Lilibet.
Piers Morgan, a British TV host, criticized Harry's remarks on Fox News, calling them hypocritical.
ai.unknown: It is not clear whether any meeting or steps toward reconciliation with Charles or William have been arranged.

ai.headline: Meta reports Q3 results as a New Mexico $25 billion penalty lands
ai.summary:
Interest in Meta stock is rising around two developments that landed on the same day. Meta was scheduled to release its third-quarter results after the market closed on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, the first major report of Big Tech's earnings season. Analysts polled by Bloomberg expected earnings of about $3.56 per share and revenue near $63.3 billion, compared with $1.05 per share and $51.2 billion a year earlier. Capital spending was projected to rise roughly 117% to $41 billion, and Reality Labs was expected to post an operating loss of about $5.2 billion. Investors are watching closely because Meta is one of the largest AI spenders, and Bloomberg reported that a weak result could add to existing worries about the AI trade.

Separately, a New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in penalties, according to a court filing reported by CNBC. The case stems from the Cambridge Analytica scandal and a September jury finding that the company misled state residents about data privacy and the handling of harmful content. The jury counted more than 43 million violations under the state's unfair practices law, with a maximum of $5,000 each, but the judge set the final amount, which was reduced from a much larger figure the filing cited. The judge also said interest would accrue at 15% a year until the fine is paid. CNBC said it had contacted Meta for comment, and the company's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
key_points: Meta was set to report third-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday, October 21.
Bloomberg analyst consensus expected about $3.56 EPS and $63.3 billion in revenue, versus $1.05 and $51.2 billion a year earlier.
Projected capital expenditures were about $41 billion, up roughly 117% year over year.
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over privacy and consumer-protection violations, according to CNBC.
The penalty is tied to the Cambridge Analytica scandal; the judge set interest at 15% a year until paid.
ai.unknown: It is not yet clear how Meta will respond to the $25 billion penalty, whether it will appeal, or how the quarterly results will be received by investors.

ai.headline: LASK come back to beat Sporting CP 3-2 in Champions League
ai.summary:
LASK earned their first Champions League win with a comeback over Sporting CP, a result that ended Sporting's unbeaten start to the competition. Sporting went ahead in the fifth minute from a Luis Suarez penalty, which the referee awarded after a foul on Nestory Irankunda. Christoph Lang equalised for LASK about ten minutes later with a low finish from the edge of the box. The visitors took control after the break. Sasa Kalajdzic scored in the 63rd minute, and Krystof Danek added a second on a counter-attack. Suarez pulled one back late for Sporting, but LASK held on.

The win was LASK's first away victory in Europe's top club competition. Before this match, the Austrian side had lost eight straight away games in major European competition, according to BBC Sport. Sporting's next match is at Shakhtar Donetsk on 3 November, which is being played at Stamford Bridge, while LASK host Slovan Bratislava the same evening. Other headlines on the match were also circulating, but the available details come mainly from the BBC report, and they are limited to the score, scorers and fixtures listed there.
key_points: LASK beat Sporting CP 3-2 in a Champions League match on 21 October.
Suarez gave Sporting a fifth-minute lead from a penalty; Christoph Lang equalised for LASK.
Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek scored for LASK in the second half; Suarez pulled one back late.

ai.headline: Angels part ways with Kurt Suzuki after a 100-loss season
ai.summary:
The Los Angeles Angels will not bring back Kurt Suzuki as manager for 2027, the club announced on a Wednesday, and they declined the option on his contract. Suzuki managed the team for one season, which ended with the franchise's first 100-loss campaign. The organization offered him a special assistant role instead, and it plans to hire a new manager and coaching staff.

Interim general manager John Mozeliak had earlier said he hoped to keep Suzuki, but he noted that the decision would rest with incoming ownership. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment is expected to finalize its purchase of the club in early 2027. Mozeliak has said Suzuki earned respect in the clubhouse, though he also said the team's record did not fully reflect Suzuki's ability. Suzuki, 43, is the first Hawaiian-born manager in MLB history, according to MLB.com. Several outlets, including ESPN and CBS Sports, reported the decision as well. It is still unclear whether Mozeliak will remain as GM when his contract expires in December.

ai.headline: New Mexico sues Epstein's former lawyer and accountant over alleged cover-up
ai.summary:
New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez filed a civil lawsuit on Wednesday against Darren Indyke, Jeffrey Epstein's longtime attorney, and Richard Kahn, his longtime accountant. The complaint, filed in federal court in New Mexico, accuses the two men of helping hide Epstein's crimes. It names both men personally and in their roles as co-executors of Epstein's estate. The filing also names the estate itself and a trust that holds its assets. The state wants a court order that would stop the two men from collecting payments from the estate while the case moves forward.

The case centers on Zorro Ranch, Epstein's property in Stanley, New Mexico. According to the complaint, Epstein and his associates abused survivors at the ranch and other locations. The lawsuit also claims the advisers received large salaries and gifts in return for staying silent. Court papers say Indyke received more than $16 million from Epstein and related entities from 2011 to 2019, and Kahn received more than $10 million over that period. Indyke and Kahn have denied knowing about or helping with Epstein's abuse. Their attorney called the suit baseless. Earlier this year, the two men told a House committee they were unaware of Epstein's crimes.
key_points: New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez filed the civil suit in federal court in New Mexico.
The suit accuses Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn of facilitating and concealing Jeffrey Epstein's crimes.
The complaint asks a court to block the two men from receiving estate payments during the case.
The suit alleges Indyke received over $16 million and Kahn over $10 million from Epstein-linked sources between 2011 and 2019.
Indyke and Kahn deny any knowledge of or involvement in the abuse; their lawyers call the suit baseless.
CNN reported that Epstein's will left Indyke $50 million and Kahn $25 million; their attorneys say payments would come only after creditors are paid and probate ends.
ai.unknown: It is unclear how the court will rule on the request to halt estate payments, and the outcome of the separate reported federal investigation of the two men has not been made public.

ai.headline: Kim Kardashian dressed as daughter North West for Halloween
ai.summary:
Searches for North West's age tie back to recent coverage of her mother's Halloween costume. Several outlets, including Sports Illustrated and E! News, report that North is 13 years old. Her mother, Kim Kardashian, shares her with ex-husband Kanye "Ye" West, and the two also have three younger children: Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7.

Kardashian drew attention by dressing as North in October, posting a costume that included a bright blue wig, black-and-white clothing, piercings and detailed nails. Coverage says the look was a near-twin of her daughter's style, and Kardashian has said she lets North experiment with her personal style, including hair color. Kardashian turned 46 on October 21, according to Sports Illustrated.
key_points: North West is 13 years old, according to Sports Illustrated and E! News.
She is the eldest child of Kim Kardashian and Kanye "Ye" West.
Kardashian's younger children are Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7.
Kardashian posted a Halloween costume channeling North, including a blue wig and piercings.
Kardashian said she allows North to experiment with hair color and personal style.
ai.unknown: Coverage does not describe North's exact birth date, so her precise age on any given day is not confirmed by these reports.

ai.headline: Oregon coach removed after team won 63-0 with onside kicks
ai.summary:
Marist Catholic High School in Eugene, Oregon, removed head varsity football coach Zach Loboy after a Friday game against Cottage Grove. According to KVAL, the team led 63-0 and the coaches and officials chose not to play the second half. The first half reportedly included at least two onside kicks, which drew criticism for running up the score. Jake Lowther, who joined the staff this year after serving as a varsity assistant at Cascade High School, will serve as interim head coach for the remaining three regular-season games, the school said.

The school's principal, Bob Fraley, said the change was needed to match the school's mission and values, and said the priority is supporting players and finishing the season well. The New York Times, through a report from The Athletic, also covered the firing, but only its headline was available for this summary, so its details could not be checked. Other search interest may relate to a separate Yahoo Sports story about Buffalo Bills fourth-quarter touchdowns and a local award story, but those reports were not available beyond their headlines. It is not yet clear from the available reporting whether the onside kicks were called by Loboy or whether any further action will follow from the school or the league.

ai.headline: Marine Corps Marathon runners get race-week prep advice from champion
ai.summary:
The Marine Corps Marathon is in Washington, D.C., this year, and WTOP News published race-week preparation tips from Tessa Barrett, a reigning women's division champion who lives in Arlington, Virginia. Barrett, who has won the race back to back, said hydration matters most, and she recommended water along with electrolyte drinks. She advised resting in the days before the race, eating plenty of carbohydrates in the two days leading up to it, and getting good sleep, especially the Friday night before.

On race day, Barrett said runners should eat at least two to three hours before the start, and she suggested taking in fluids and carbohydrates while running, roughly every 20 to 30 minutes depending on body size. She also said energy gels should be taken at the 5K, 10K and halfway points rather than later in the race. According to WTOP, the Interstate 395 bridge near mile 20 is known for cramping runners, and the first few miles have the most elevation change. Axios also published a headline saying the race takes over D.C. this weekend, but its report contains no further details in this summary.
key_points: Tessa Barrett, a back-to-back women's division champion from Arlington, Virginia, shared race prep tips with WTOP News.
Barrett recommended hydration with water and electrolyte drinks as the top priority before the race.
She advised eating a meal at least two to three hours before the start and fueling during the run every 20 to 30 minutes.
WTOP reports the Interstate 395 bridge around mile 20 is known for cramping runners.
The race expo is at the National Building Museum in D.C., according to WTOP.

ai.headline: Justice Department sues over Alaska Senate certification if Sullivan loses
ai.summary:
The Trump administration has asked a court to hold up certification of Alaska's U.S. Senate election if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan is defeated, according to CNN. The filing, made before the November vote, targets a second candidate also named Daniel J. Sullivan, whom the lawsuit says could confuse voters. CNN reports that state election officials listed him without a party label, while Sen. Sullivan appears on the ballot as a registered Republican and incumbent. In the primary, Sen. Sullivan received 68,726 votes and the second Sullivan received 4,107, according to CNN.

The case matters for control of the Senate because Democrats need a net gain of four seats, and Alaska is among the Republican-held states they are targeting. Sen. Sullivan is running against Democrat Mary Peltola in a race that has drawn little reliable polling. CNN reports that the lawsuit relies on a federal voter registration law's stated goal of protecting the integrity of elections, and that a Notre Dame law professor, Derek Muller, called the legal theory unusual. Headlines from Politico, Axios, CBS News, The Washington Post and WPTZ describe the same lawsuit, with some saying the suit would act if the incumbent narrowly loses. President Trump posted on Truth Social that the second candidate amounted to cheating.
key_points: The Justice Department sued to block certification of Alaska's Senate election if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses.
A second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan is on the ballot; state officials listed him without a party affiliation.
In the primary, Dan Sullivan received 68,726 votes and Daniel J. Sullivan received 4,107, per CNN.
Democrats need a net gain of four seats in November, and Alaska is one of their targets.
Legal experts quoted by CNN say the lawsuit's theory is unusual and unclear in how a court could act.

ai.headline: UK grid operator says lights will stay on this winter
ai.summary:
Britain's electricity grid operator, the National Energy System Operator (NESO), says supplies should remain secure through the coming winter. It described the system as prepared and resilient, while also warning that some days could be tight. If that happens, NESO will send notices to power producers asking them to possibly add generation. NESO says such notices are routine and are not warnings of blackouts.

The forecasts come amid scrutiny of Britain's energy position. An independent investigation by the law firm Eversheds Sutherland reported high stress and concern among staff in NESO's control room about keeping supply balanced, partly because renewable power is less flexible than gas. National Gas, a private company that runs the country's gas network, said it expects enough supply to meet demand, though it expects more gas use for power at peak times. Separately, reports say Britain may pay higher prices than neighboring markets to import energy, and gas stores in Britain are small compared with many European countries.
key_points: NESO says Britain's electricity system is prepared and secure for winter
NESO warns some days may be tight and will issue routine notices to generators, not blackout warnings
An independent investigation found high stress among control room staff about supply
National Gas expects sufficient gas supply but more gas use for power at peak demand
Britain is expected to import more power and pay higher prices to secure supply, according to reports
ai.unknown: It is not yet clear whether any tight days will occur this winter or how often NESO will need to issue notices.

The race has an expo held at the National Building Museum, where runners pick up race materials before the event. Many people running it are doing so for the first time.

Race preparation is a common topic before the event. WTOP News recently published tips from Tessa Barrett, a reigning women's division champion who lives in Arlington, Virginia, and has won the race back to back. She said hydration is the top priority, and she recommended water along with electrolyte drinks. She also advised resting the legs in the days before the race, eating plenty of carbohydrates in the two days leading up to it, and getting good sleep, especially the night before the Saturday race. On race day, she said runners should eat at least two to three hours before the start, then take in fluids and carbohydrates while running, roughly every 20 to 30 minutes. She suggested taking energy gels at the 5K, 10K and halfway points rather than later.

The course is described by Barrett as fair, with most of its elevation change in the first few miles. She noted that the Interstate 395 bridge near mile 20 is a spot where runners often experience cramps. Route, map and road closure details are not covered in the sources used for this page, so readers should check the official race website for those.

katarzyna-kawa.subject: Katarzyna Kawa
katarzyna-kawa.title: Who is Katarzyna Kawa?
katarzyna-kawa.answer: Katarzyna Kawa is a professional tennis player from Poland, ranked No. 128 in the WTA rankings. She is the opponent Elena Rybakina faces next at the BNB Ningbo Open quarterfinals in China, after Kawa beat 14th-seeded Belinda Bencic.
katarzyna-kawa.body:
Katarzyna Kawa is a tennis player who competes on the WTA Tour, the top professional women's tour. She entered the BNB Ningbo Open as a qualifier, meaning she came through the qualifying rounds to reach the main draw. WTA Tennis describes her as an unlikely qualifier and says she is 33 years old. She made her WTA Tour debut in 2010, and this year's Ningbo run is the first time she has beaten a top-20 player, according to WTA Tennis.

In her previous match, Kawa beat Belinda Bencic, the 14th seed, 7-5, 6-2. WTA Tennis reports that Kawa has won four matches in Ningbo this week, including two second-set walkovers in qualifying and a comeback first-round win over Daria Snigur, 1-6, 6-2, 6-4. Kawa said after the Bencic win that she had no particular expectations and was excited for her next match.

Her next match is against Elena Rybakina, the world No. 1 and top seed, who reached the quarterfinals after her second-round opponent, Polina Kudermetova, retired with a right shoulder injury while trailing 5-0 in the first set. WTA Tennis notes that this will be the first meeting between the two players and that Rybakina has not yet completed a set in Ningbo this week.

pro-and-tell-apple-event.answer: "Pro and tell" is the name Apple has given to a product launch event on October 28 in Los Angeles. The name is a play on the MacBook Pro laptop line. Apple confirmed the date, location and name, and says new hardware will be shown there.
pro-and-tell-apple-event.body:
Apple is a technology company that designs computers, phones and tablets. Companies like Apple often hold product launch events to introduce new devices and software to the public. The name of this one, "Pro and tell," is a wordplay on the MacBook Pro, Apple's line of higher-end laptops, in the same way "show and tell" is a classroom activity.

Apple confirmed on Monday, October 19, 2026, that the event will be held on October 28 in Los Angeles. According to Bloomberg's reporting, the main expected debut is Apple's first touch-screen MacBook. Bloomberg also reports that Apple may introduce a lower-priced MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, an updated iMac, and a revised iPad mini with a sharper display. Apple has not confirmed these product details; they come from Bloomberg's reporting.
